generated.runtime: tsc emit of upstream/src modules minus the excluded feature surfaces (auto-read-all, config-ui, copy-move, glob, grep; the package entry index.ts is vendored but never compiled or loaded), compiled with upstream's own ESNext/bundler options, then mechanically rewritten to Node-loadable ESM specifiers (./x -> ./x.js, ./dir -> ./dir/index.js, JSON imports gain with { type: "json" }), then OMA divergence splices applied

file-kind.js.reason: OMA read seam: the whole file load — sniff sample and body — goes through one injectable opener. In a host engine the adapter installs the contained opener (workspace/readable-root admission plus the descriptor-relative no-follow walk), so a hashline read cannot reach a path the workspace guard would refuse. Uninstalled, upstream's plain fs open is the behavior — the seam adds authority routing, never weakens it.

file-kind.d.ts.reason: Declaration for the file-kind.js OMA read seam (see the .js divergence) so the adapter's installer call type-checks under NodeNext.

fs-write.js.reason: OMA write seam, fail-closed: the two commit paths (commit.js and batch.js's multi-edit close) are rerouted from upstream's writeAtomic to an installed writer, and the read-back verification read is rerouted to the same seam's read. OMA's adapter installs the contained serialized writer — quota decided inside the serialization, no-follow descriptor walks, inode-identity check against the read snapshot. With no channel installed the seam throws instead of falling back to readFile/writeAtomic — a missing channel means the contained boundary was never wired, and a silent fallback would read or write the mutation target outside it. writeAtomic itself is kept but confined to the bundle's own state directory (config.js's configPath() under configDir(), redirected by the adapter into OMA-owned space via PI_HASHLINE_DIR — a different ownership domain); any other direct writeAtomic target — e.g. replace-undo.js's undo write, were that tool ever registered — refuses closed instead of writing uncontained. The identity contract is upstream's: a missing or replaced inode refuses before a byte is written.

fs-write.d.ts.reason: Declarations for the fs-write.js OMA commit seam (see the .js divergence): the installed channel's read/write pair and the commit/verification entry points the rerouted callers use.

commit.js.reason: Commit reroute: the unchanged-since-plan verification read and the final write go through the installed OMA commit channel instead of node:fs readFile and upstream writeAtomic. Semantics kept: the content is compared after stripBOM/toLF exactly as upstream, and the write still carries the read snapshot's inode identity so a replaced or deleted target refuses before writing.

batch.js.reason: Batch commit reroute: the multi-edit close's verification re-read and final write take the same OMA commit channel as commit.js — contained admission, serialized quota decision, inode-identity check — rather than node:fs readFile and upstream writeAtomic.

generated.upstreamTests: upstream-tests/ is the repository's test/ tree at the vendored commit (the npm tarball ships no tests); kept for provenance and porting, not wired into npm test — they need vitest and the upstream ../src layout
